question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The size of Jupiter and Mars is similar.
The density of Saturn is similar to that of Earth.
The size of Earth and Venus is almost similar.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option** **4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Earth and Venus are often referred to as "sister planets" due to their similar sizes, with Earth having a diameter of about 12,742 km and Venus around 12,104 km.
 
• Mars is not the warmest planet; Venus is the hottest due to its thick atmosphere that traps heat.
 
• Saturn has a much lower density than Earth. Saturn is the least dense planet in the solar system, with a density less than that of water.
 
• Jupiter is significantly larger than Mars; in fact, it is the largest planet in our solar system, while Mars is much smaller.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jupiter's diameter** is about 139,822 km, making it more than **6 **times larger than Earth.
 
• **Mars **has a **thin atmosphere** and average temperatures around -80 degrees Fahrenheit (-62 degrees Celsius), much colder than Earth.
 
• **Venus **has a dense atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide, contributing to its **extreme greenhouse effect** and surface temperatures around 900 degrees Fahrenheit (475 degrees Celsius).
 
• **Saturn **is famous for its prominent** ring system**, which is made up of ice and rock particles ranging in size.
 
• While Earth is a rocky planet, both Venus and Mars are also terrestrial, but they differ significantly in terms of surface conditions and atmospheres.
 
• Earth has a stronger **gravitational pull** compared to Mars and Venus due to its larger mass, affecting the potential for retaining an atmosphere and sustaining life.
